description: Technical University of Munich and Fraunhofer IOSB provide a repeated airborne laser-scanning benchmark for Abenberg, Germany, for change-detection development and evaluation and city modelling. The provider locates the test site at 49.2416 N, 10.9636 E. Four crossing flight strips acquired in April 2008 produced 5.4 million points with an average density of 16 points per square metre. The site was scanned again in August 2009 using the same sensors and a similar acquisition setting. The source states that three-dimensional coordinates are accompanied by sensor positions, local normal directions and pre-classification results. The two dated acquisitions are grouped as one repeated-survey benchmark, not separate new datasets. This source-established city-modelling role supports reconstruction and comparison of built-environment geometry. Public download links are listed for two ZIP archives, described as 111 MB and 147 MB. The original ALS dataset is available under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; the page does not state a charge. A limitation is that internal file formats, coordinate reference system, registration quality and the second acquisition point count were not established from the inspected metadata. Spatial coverage is the Abenberg test site; the average 2008 point density is not a uniform accuracy guarantee. The two observations are snapshots, with no continuing update schedule stated. Related MLS benchmarks occur in the same provider directory but are distinct sites and acquisition methods. No archive, README, point data, image or article body was retrieved.
